headline: When to Repair or Replace Your Damaged Stairs
articleBody: It's a common dilemma: when do you patch up your existing stairs, and when is it time for a full replacement? Generally, smaller issues like loose treads, minor cracks, or worn finishes can often be repaired. If the damage is mostly cosmetic and doesn't affect the stability or safety of the stairs, a skilled repair can bring them back to life. However, if you're seeing more serious signs such as significant sagging, widespread cracking, persistent movement, or visible rot, you're likely looking at a structural problem that may warrant a more extensive repair or even a complete rebuild. These are the kinds of issues where professional help isn't just a good idea, it's essential for safety and code compliance. Things like tread and riser dimensions, as well as handrail height, are all subject to building codes, and getting these wrong can lead to hazards. For example, common limits often cite a 7-inch maximum riser height and handrail heights between 34-38 inches above the nosing. A professional can assess the extent of the damage, determine if a permit is needed, and ensure any repairs or replacements meet these critical safety standards. We serve the East Bay Area, including communities like Berkeley, Oakland, and Alameda, and can provide the expertise needed to make the right call for your home.
